title: FLAGSHIP: BNT vs non-BNT at matched lmax=460 (MOPED, pooled)
note: THE FLAGSHIP CONSTRAINING-POWER RESULT. Both arms score/MOPED-compressed at the SAME scale cut (lmax=460, rebin=20, hybrid covariance, 5 NDE seeds each), so the only difference between them is the BNT basis: BNT cuts bin-1 only and keeps bins 2-4 to lmax=1024 (92 of 120 columns), non-BNT cuts every bin (50 of 120). BNT gives 1.47x the 3-parameter FoM. Both posteriors are calibrated (SBC rank-std 0.28-0.29 against the ideal 0.289) and on-truth (null means within 0.3 sigma), and both are unbiased at this cut (baryon tension 0.30+/-0.09 sigma for BNT, 0.17+/-0.03 for non-BNT), which is what makes the matched comparison fair. Read this as constraining power at fixed cut, NOT as baryon mitigation: BNT bin-1 actually crosses 0.3 sigma at a LOWER lmax (460) than non-BNT cut-all (620), so cutting only bin 1 does not control baryons better - it retains more information at equal unbiasedness. The 1.47x is also conditional on the compression: under raw NPE the same comparison inverts to 0.33x, because a flow fed the ill-conditioned BNT vector loses the Omega_m-S8 degeneracy entirely (r=-0.03 against the physical -0.9) while passing every standard calibration check.
